title: Add --features flag to cargo test invocations for targets with required-features

invented_rule.summary: cargo test --all-targets silently skips integration test targets that declare required-features in Cargo.toml; every cargo test invocation for such a package must explicitly pass --features <feature> or the tests silently do not run, giving a false-green signal.
invented_rule.absent_from_pretraining_rationale: The specific behavior that cargo --all-targets silently skips required-features targets (exit 0, no compilation, no tests run) is a non-obvious cargo quirk. Pretraining on general Rust/cargo documentation would not reliably surface that --all-targets is incomplete for required-features tests, and a generic solver fixing a CI script would not know to audit for this silent omission.

prompt:
The CI script `ci.sh` runs cargo tests for the `mcp-server` crate. The `Cargo.toml` shows that the integration test target `test_live_data_plane_roundtrip` has `required-features = ["test-utils"]`. The current script runs:

```bash
cargo test -p mcp-server --test test_live_data_plane_roundtrip -- --ignored
```

This silently exits 0 without compiling or running any tests because the `test-utils` feature is not passed. Fix `ci.sh` so the integration tests actually compile and run.

setup:
cat > Cargo.toml << 'TOMLEOF'
[package]
name = "mcp-server"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[features]
test-utils = []

[[test]]
name = "test_live_data_plane_roundtrip"
path = "tests/test_live_data_plane_roundtrip.rs"
required-features = ["test-utils"]
TOMLEOF

cat > ci.sh << 'SHEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Run live integration tests
cargo test -p mcp-server --test test_live_data_plane_roundtrip -- --ignored
SHEOF

verifier.contract: Invoked as `<command> <workspace_dir>`. Exit 0 == invented rule OBEYED (task win). Non-zero == rule NOT obeyed. MUST print a one-line human reason to stdout. NO network, NO LLM — pure deterministic inspection of the produced workspace/diff.

expected.sensitivity_note: If ON fails this with the rule injected (attribution confirms the pull), that is INSTRUMENT-FAILURE.
